title: Certifying smoke runs of the study: does a coding agent's model need to re-read its own reasoning?
description:
The certifying smoke set of study for model reasoning visibility, a pre-registered study of whether an AI coding agent's model needs to see its own earlier reasoning again. Each of eight open-weight models (Gemma-4-31B-it, Qwen3.6-27B, Seed-OSS-36B-Instruct, gpt-oss-20b, GLM-4.7-Flash, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, Gemma-4-26B-A4B-it, Muse Glimmer 30B) builds two small web apps under three tool conditions, in up to three arms: thinking OFF, thinking on with past reasoning discarded (UNSEEN), and thinking on with past reasoning replayed (SEEN).

The set holds 66 agent runs made on 2026-10-07 from harness commit 5ac366f4175dc0929c28ad45e1560d26760f83fa (tag model-reasoning-visibility-study-freeze-100826), served by llama.cpp b10964. For each run it keeps the workspace the agent built, the full request/response trace, the run manifest, the console log, the command list, the toolchain record and the model server's log at its most detailed level (zstd-compressed). It also includes the gate script that certified the set (verify_smokes.py), its output, the decoding registry it checks against, and the batch runner's schedule and progress records.

These runs are not study data. The protocol excludes every smoke and probe run from analysis; they are published so that the frozen settings can be checked against what the runs actually did. See README.md for the layout and how to re-run the gates.
notes: Smoke runs of a pre-registered study; excluded from its analysis by design. Harness commit 5ac366f4175dc0929c28ad45e1560d26760f83fa; node_modules folders are not included and are rebuilt from each package-lock.json with npm ci.
